````text
# Documentation and validation workflow

1. Freeze the current local HTML identity and publication commit. Preserve the original application.
2. Retrieve published Zenodo metadata. Compare all 17 manual bytes against published MD5 values, then calculate SHA-256.
3. Extract every PDF page and retain page-level provenance. Read historical validation limitations and inspect evidence ZIPs.
4. Reconstruct the current HTML from its manifest and require an exact byte match. Parse JavaScript with Node-bundled Acorn 8.18.0.
5. Index first-party and dependency function nodes separately. Compare canonical AST bodies with the archived HTML; retain ambiguous matches.
6. Instrument only a separate review HTML for function-entry counts. Run supplied suites against it. Preserve initial failures, test-only harness adjustments and subsequent results.
7. Attribute passing scenario IDs to functions without equating entry with correctness. Preserve unobserved code as a review gap.
8. Write current wiki chapters, archive inventories, change crosswalk and limitations. Do not rewrite old results as current results.
9. Package source, scripts, results and review questions. Exclude credentials and private instrument fixtures. Calculate hashes on exact delivered bytes.

## Reproduction entry points

- `index_missy_manuals.py`: historical PDF text/provenance indexing.
- `gather_wiki_evidence.py`: evidence archive acquisition and identity checks.
- `index_current_missy_functions.cjs`: exact build reconstruction, AST indexing and test-only instrumentation.
- `run_current_missy_validation.cjs`: initial suite run.
- `retest_current_missy.cjs`: selected reruns after preserved test-harness adjustments.
- `build_missy_documentation.py`: documentation and evidence crosswalk generation.

The scripts currently retain absolute Windows paths. For another computer, edit the declared input roots and Playwright location, supply lawful instrument fixtures, and reproduce the same dependency versions. Missing fixture/password coverage is explicitly incomplete. No credentials are supplied.

## Hash method

All SHA-256 values in SHA256SUMS.txt hash the complete raw bytes of the named file, without JSON canonicalisation or line-ending conversion. SHA256SUMS.txt excludes itself. This is independent of any application-internal identity field.

## R2 follow-up

Read R2_SCOPE.md and CLEAN_CONFIRMATION.md. Repaired fixtures/tests are in reproduction/missy_modular. Run generate_zip_fixtures.py then the two tests, followed by run_clean_missy_validation_r2.cjs for all 24 suites. No coverage preload is used. Original failures and R1 counters remain preserved. Audio provenance is linked by exact asset hash, not inferred from encoder tags.

````

[Complete record](https://github.com/mihaiionitabio-alt/zpcrweb/blob/missy-public-offline-2026-10-20/documentation/releases/2026-10-31-full-wiki/validation/current/R2_SCOPE.md)

````text
# R2 scope and review disposition

Production HTML is unchanged. Production source files are compared with the R1 source snapshot in SOURCE_UNCHANGED.json. Test-only changes and diffs are retained.

## ZIP

The missing fixture is replaced by a committed deterministic Python generator and a manifest of eleven invented ZIP files. The test boots the entire frozen HTML and calls the actual public readZip/readZipFiltered functions. It tests default/explicit filters, UTF-8 paths, stored and deflated members, CRC mismatch, unsupported method, malformed archive, declared member size limit and decoded-size mismatch. It stages/reads artificial RDML and compares wells, analyses, cycle count and curves against the same direct XML bytes; threshold cycle 25.5 is checked explicitly.

Intake expanded-byte and file-count guards use temporarily reduced in-memory test budgets; defaults are restored in finally. The member-size test uses the actual 512 MiB declared-size threshold without allocating that payload. The count guard currently retains the first accepted member and reports the error. Tests assert that behaviour rather than falsely claiming atomic rejection.

A ../ path is accepted as virtual source metadata and its basename is used. No archive member is extracted to the operating-system filesystem. There is no traversal-rejection guard to claim as passed. This should be reconsidered if disk extraction is ever added.

This synthetic suite does not replace the missing historical native batch archives, CFX archive-manifest binding checks, mixed-endianness ICFF payload quirks, variable thermal headers, undeclared compression, ZIP64/encryption or successful PCRD decryption. Separate direct-reader regression suites are not substitutes for those archive-specific cases.

## MARA

All 32 current MARA_PROFILE_LIBRARY entries are checked against pinned production sopHash values. The normal test cannot rewrite the oracle. Explicit oracle recording is available only through MISSY_RECORD_MARA_ORACLE=1 and was performed after asserting Positive outcomes and raw-record immutability for all mathematical fixtures. These baseline outcomes are regression oracles, not an independent determination that the standards were implemented correctly.

Each entry is evaluated through sopEvaluateRun with explicitly supplied curve evidence and context. The test checks failed acceptance checks, decision code/outcome and unchanged raw records, then exercises bilingual profile loading, JSON save/import and ZIP export. The removed SC preset is not restored. Synthetic fixture profile adaptations are separate from the pinned shipped profile hashes.

## PCRD and log differences

The keyboard suite cancels password-required PCRD input when no password fixture is provided. A pass is evidence of keyboard navigation/cancellation only, not decrypted data or pcrdCRC/pcrdDecryptContainer correctness. R1 entry counters remain unchanged; clean contract evidence is linked separately.

Initial run_ logs and clean_ logs did not merely differ because of preload output: voice mocks were fixed between attempts, Playwright require paths changed, and PCRD cancellation was introduced. For MARA, the initial failure was a missing runtime path; the next failure was the removed SC accessor. Compare run_, retest_, clean_ and clean_r2_ with HARNESS_ADJUSTMENTS.json. The first R2 keyboard attempt exceeded its 180-second process allowance; its log/result is retained. A separate clean retry uses a 600-second allowance and is combined by suite ID only in CLEAN_R2_FINAL_RESULTS.json. R2 logs are a new attempt; old logs are not rewritten.

## Remaining review findings

Use only the frozen dist build, never a browser Save Page/DOM snapshot that may contain extension scripts or loaded session state. Recorded audio provenance and redistribution terms remain unresolved pending creation-time evidence. The catalogue is exposed as window.MISSY_COMPUTER_SOUND.catalog; use .length to check the 515-entry count. Download pseudonymisation does not govern spoken names. Baseline AST matching is many-to-one, not an unchanged-function cardinality.
````

````text
MISSY qPCR QC and forensics - release 2026.10.17

Open index.html locally in a modern browser. Single-file application; no installation needed.
Live application: https://mihaiionitabio-alt.github.io/lc480-ixo-qc-exportv2/
Repository: https://github.com/mihaiionitabio-alt/lc480-ixo-qc-exportv2

DOCUMENTATION
The original 6437-page manual is provided in 17 PDF volumes, split only at chapter boundaries. Every chapter stays complete. All original pages, numbering and artwork are preserved. The later patch supplement documents fixes made after the 7 October manual. A volume-to-chapter/page map is in screenshot_catalogue_2026-10-17.zip. The original large single PDF is replaced by these complete smaller volumes for reliable upload.

ACTUAL APPLICATION SCREENSHOTS
44 page_screenshots_part ZIPs contain exactly 4000 unique, unmodified 1600x1100 Chromium page screenshots from the current index.html. These are actual rendered application pages, not generated illustrations or presentation graphics. Only the input measurements are invented synthetic fixtures. Extract all image ZIPs and screenshot_catalogue_2026-10-17.zip into one folder; open SCREENSHOT_INDEX.html to search the screenshots. The catalogue includes image SHA256 hashes, native view/experiment/options, capture report, skipped-state report and manual volume map. Separate capture tools and additional 384-well input archives support reproduction. Images retain the native viewport; longer pages can extend outside it.

DEMONSTRATION INPUTS AND VALIDATION
Three format ZIPs contain 24 IXO, 24 EDS and 48 matching RDML files. A separate drift scenario archive contains 50 IXO, 50 EDS and 100 matching RDML files. Vendor and RDML representations are not independent experiments. All new measurement values in demonstration and regression files are invented rather than anonymised laboratory observations. The synthetic-only SOP profile must not replace a real laboratory SOP.

Source code, generator/validation toolkit, regression fixtures, scoped validation evidence, usage exports, reviewed documentation source subset, release identity/citation/checksum tools and selected screenshots are also provided. The documentation source subset intentionally excludes laboratory-derived data/figures and cannot recreate the full manual. Existing documentation PDFs may describe historical laboratory work.

No raw laboratory experiments, sample-level laboratory exports, private fixture archives, laboratory-calibrated reconstruction datasets, credentials or separately distributed proprietary fonts are included. These software and import checks do not establish calibrated statistical or clinical performance.

Verify every downloaded file with SHA256SUMS.txt. The checksum manifest covers all other files in this record. The record remains a draft until separately authorised for publication.
````

````text
SYNTHETIC DEMO AND VALIDATION TOOLS - 2026.10.17

Three ZIPs: 24 IXO + 24 EDS + 48 RDML files: all are generated from invented identifiers and measurements, with no real laboratory run as input. RDML files are matching representations of the all 24 runs per platform; do not count both formats as independent experiments. Load IXO and EDS for hardware demos. RDML cannot preserve all proprietary hardware telemetry.

Download all .py tools into one folder. Imports were flattened for Zenodo individual downloads; generator logic is unchanged. Generator uses Python standard library. Verifiers require Python Playwright and Chromium:
 python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
 python -m playwright install chromium

Generate a fresh set and full matching RDML set:
 python generate.py demo --scale 1 --only LC96,QS96 --rdml demo_rdml
Generate trends:
 python generate.py drift --only LCDRIFT,QSDRIFT --drift-runs 50
Verify (supply your local index.html path):
 python verify.py index.html demo --no-exports --json report.json
 python verify.py index.html demo --self-test
 python verify_drift.py index.html drift

MANIFEST.tsv and EXPECTED.tsv describe the 48 vendor runs. Keep them alongside the vendor inputs for verifier runs. Synthetic scenarios deliberately include abnormal values: they are software tests, not calibration materials or manufacturer-certified runs. For RDML-only verification use an appropriate matching expectation subset rather than the full vendor expectation file.

Current release evidence: all 96 generated files imported with nonempty wells and zero browser errors. See SYNTHETIC_IMPORT_SMOKE_RESULTS.json for application checksum. This is an import smoke check; full current-build scenario correctness, graphs, exports, forecasts and statistical calibration are not established. The broader verification tools predate the newest sample-selection and duration-chart additions.

At least 20 matching vendor runs are generally needed for a default baseline. These vendor cohorts each contain 24 runs; individual metric availability and SOP eligibility still apply. Each RDML platform has 24 runs, but vendor hardware-only metrics need the corresponding IXO/EDS inputs.

DEMO SOP PROFILE: SYNTHETIC_DEMO_ONLY_SOP_PROFILE.json reclassifies LEC as an internal control and fixes its reference Cq at 23 for chart demonstrations. It changes interpretation rules and must not be used for laboratory samples.
````

pages.title: ChartsAndEvidence
pages.text:
# Charts and evidence

The current registry contains **83 control-chart definitions** and **25 single-run graph definitions**. These counts describe available definitions; each input file may support only some of them.

Read the plotted quantity, channel, run/acquisition scope, units, baseline minimum and limits before interpreting a point. A chart without sufficient baseline or declared limits cannot be called a pass merely because no point is flagged.

Review amplification, plate/sample associations, instrument records, stored results and rising curves without a same-channel result. A flag describes an observed rule violation, not its biological or hardware cause.

Default dark charts and optional white backgrounds support screen review. Numbered voice chart requests use the focused Console view with a way to restore headers and controls.


[Wiki home](/p/zpcrweb/wiki/Home/)

pages.title: CurrentBuildChanges
pages.text:
# Changes from the archived manual

The archived October 17 HTML has SHA-256 `e2e4b58082386e77e1c125e962e426439fdb0bddbbc5378e34b15e5c956b67fc`. The current local HTML has SHA-256 `d2ed246783339c8153db567872cc5baafbcde9e7be477db5981ea22521b68b0c` and is 28,081,180 bytes. Local CRLF bytes and the Git LF-normalised blob have different hashes; compare like with like.

The current bundle has 135 manifest modules. AST indexing identifies 6,180 first-party function nodes and 5,552 dependency function nodes. Within first-party code, 756 named nodes have no historical name match, 73 have a changed uniquely matched name, 187 have ambiguous name matches and 1,724 are new or changed anonymous nodes. 3,440 have an equivalent historical function body. These categories describe code comparison, not feature quality or scientific correctness.

The manual needs current chapters for ZPCR/PCRD readers, expanded forensic evidence, precision disclosure, browser capability messages, LCARS layout, session/workspace selection, the second voice demo, the learning game and reports, command recognition/response sequencing and the expanded sound system. Historical chart atlases remain examples of their own build rather than screenshots of today's interface.

This update supplies a current documentation layer and machine-readable crosswalk; it does not overwrite the historical 17-volume record.

AST matching counts current functions matching a historical body and permits multiple current matches to one baseline body. It is not a one-to-one count of unchanged functions.


[Wiki home](/p/zpcrweb/wiki/Home/)

pages.title: DataFormats
pages.text:
# Data formats and provenance

The public interface accepts IXO, EDS/EDT, RDML, ZPCR, PCRD and ZIP containers. Seven regression groups separate ordinary RDML from Bio-Rad-exported RDML. A format name does not guarantee every vendor revision or optional field is supported.

Keep acquired fluorescence, vendor-reported results and independently calculated results distinct. Missing values must remain missing. A rising curve in one channel is not a replacement threshold cycle for another channel. An unnamed reaction may still carry real stored data.

QuantStudio checks compare sample/target associations, Rn and ΔRn, threshold cycles, quantities and melting results against available exports. A limited export does not establish the meaning of absent fields.

Encrypted PCRD requires the relevant password. Current cancellation tests establish graceful handling of locked files, not successful decryption of all PCRD variants. Original laboratory fixtures and credentials are not included in the review bundle.


[Wiki home](/p/zpcrweb/wiki/Home/)

pages.title: DemosAndLearning
pages.text:
# Demonstrations and learning

Two demonstrations use artificial data: a **30-lesson guided tour** and a **69-step voice workflow** in three chapters. Recorded demonstrations must be checked against current answers; prerecorded speech is not proof that live microphone recognition succeeded.

The learning game has **24 lessons**, with artificial runs loaded into MISSY, highlighted evidence, simple questions, clickable evidence and typed or optional spoken answers. The current fixture contains **33 runs and 789 stored results**. It includes cycle-limit tokens, genuine final-cycle measurements and unnamed reactions with rising curves missing a result in their own channel. It excludes melting lessons.

Scores recognise the required evidence and answer. Latency can be recorded but must not reward hurried laboratory decisions. The downloadable learning report records name, laboratory, questions, evidence screenshots, score and elapsed time. It supports practice, not competency certification or replacement of supervised bench work.


[Wiki home](/p/zpcrweb/wiki/Home/)

pages.title: FunctionIndex
pages.text:
# Function index

[Complete function-by-function code and validation reference](/p/zpcrweb/wiki/CodeReference/)

The current index contains 11,732 nodes: 6,180 first-party and 5,552 dependency nodes. It includes nested callbacks and methods. Each exact function source is hash-verified; most functions are shown inline, with oversized asset-bearing functions linked in full.

[Complete source modules](/p/zpcrweb/wiki/ModuleSources/) · [Historical 705 symbol records](/p/zpcrweb/wiki/HistoricalFunctions/) · [Full validation records](/p/zpcrweb/wiki/ValidationData/)

R1 entry observations are not individual correctness proofs. R2 clean contract checks remain separate. Many current bodies can match one historical AST. Unobserved functions and unsupported cases remain explicitly marked.

pages.title: GettingStarted
pages.text:
# Getting started

1. Download the current HTML and open it in a supported modern browser.
2. Select the interface language and enter laboratory and investigator details. These fields identify the session; they are not authentication.
3. Choose **Real data analysis** or **Learning game**. The learning workspace loads artificial data and must not be confused with laboratory results.
4. Stage files, read them, and review the file summary before interpreting results.
5. Select or configure an approved laboratory SOP, review applicability and controls, and examine the evidence behind flags.
6. Export the report for that analysis and retain the build and profile identities with the original files.

Internet Explorer is unsupported. Optional offline speech recognition has narrower browser support than the core page. Browser capability messages must be followed; a Chinese interface does not install a Chinese speech voice.


[Wiki home](/p/zpcrweb/wiki/Home/)

pages.title: Limitations
pages.text:
# Limitations and licensing

MISSY is research-use software and is not validated. A laboratory must establish suitability for its own methods, instruments, data and SOPs. Feature availability does not establish ISO/IEC 17025 conformity or accreditation.

Local offline processing reduces the need to send experiment data elsewhere. It does not establish encryption, access control, backup, malware protection or secure deletion. Laboratory/investigator names are session metadata, not a login security boundary.

An outlier or failed rule does not establish contamination, inhibition, instrument failure or another cause. Missing evidence must not become an unsupported negative result. A cycle-count sentinel must remain distinct from a genuine measured threshold cycle at the same number.

Source-code, third-party library, font, documentation and audio licences must be considered individually. An open record or repository does not grant new rights to every embedded asset. The historical source subset does not include every private fixture or figure needed to reproduce the complete old book.

Download pseudonymisation does not govern speech. Spoken answers can contain identifiers regardless of the download setting and can be heard or recorded. Headphones do not make speech subject to that setting.

pages.title: ReportingAndExports
pages.text:
# Reporting and exports

Reports belong to the loaded experiment, selected SOP and identified build. Keep original data alongside the exported interpretation. Pseudonymisation and filter settings affect what is exported; retain any re-identification material separately.

Exports and screenshots have their own byte identities. A changed font or embedded audio asset can alter a file hash without changing calculations. Hashes prove matching bytes, not scientific validity, calibration or security.

Training reports are artificial-data learning records. They must not be presented as laboratory result reports or professional certification.


[Wiki home](/p/zpcrweb/wiki/Home/)

pages.title: SOPAndResults
pages.text:
# SOP and results

Applicability is evaluated before sample interpretation. A profile outside its declared method scope is **Profile not applicable**, not a negative sample result. Controls, replicate rules and the reason for an outcome must remain visible.

Laboratory owners must approve method-specific thresholds, revisions, control-name mapping and acceptance rules. A supplied template or synthetic training profile is not an approved laboratory SOP.

MARA profile metadata and mathematical tests have separate evidence. The R2 definitions test checks 32 pinned shipped-library hashes and synthetic run outcomes, alongside mathematical tests. Original failures remain in the review logs.

Review-only profiles do not authorise release. Stored values, derived results and rule conclusions must be distinguishable.


[Wiki home](/p/zpcrweb/wiki/Home/)

**3688 of 6180 first-party function nodes** were entered during passing instrumented browser scenarios. This is execution coverage, not 3688 independent correctness proofs. Static and VM tests may validate contracts without browser-entry records. Unobserved functions remain explicitly indexed.

The current checks include reader/results/export comparisons, guided and voice demos, bilingual learning/reporting, recognition state handling, read-only evidence and mathematical unit tests. PCRD password cancellation is distinct from successful decryption.

## Historical evidence: record 23437639

All seventeen published PDF files were matched to the record's MD5 checksums and all **6,437 pages** were text-indexed. The historical function volume lists 676 harness symbols plus 29 uncovered symbols; these include constants and cannot be compared directly with the current nested-function AST count.

The archived material reports 105 engine assertions, 50 panel assertions, 17 regression checks, 14 name-pattern checks, 13 selection-edge checks, 16 property checks, 27 synthetic-run checks and 89 RDML cases. These are separate historical checks, sometimes covering overlapping behaviours. Do not add them into a count of independently validated features. Duplicate regression records are not additional tests.

Archived import smoke sets contain 96 main-demo files and 200 drift files. The complete manual atlas describes 356 native synthetic runs. Matching RDML exports are representations of those runs, not independent experiments.

The screenshot archive contains 4,000 PNGs and **537 skipped states**. Skips include unavailable views and a chart-render error. Zero errors in a final resumed capture is not proof of an uninterrupted error-free capture.

The manual itself warns that a harness “pass” may mean only that a call did not throw. An inappropriate synthetic call returning NaN was still marked pass historically. Those verdicts are preserved as historical evidence, not promoted to current scientific validation.

## Later archived evidence: record 23623413

The October 24 package documents seven groups with 74 source files and 92 decoded views, plus the then-current 30-lesson demo. It is not the October 31 build. Its broader PCRD fixture coverage must not be attributed to a current locked-file cancellation test.

## Outstanding gaps

- The generated ZIP fixture now passes container guards and artificial RDML parity. Historical native archive quirks remain untested by this replacement; see R2_SCOPE.md.
- MARA definitions now checks all 32 current profiles and pinned synthetic outcomes. These are regression oracles, not laboratory validation.
- Native microphone transcription, device speaker volume, clinical performance, intended-use validation and laboratory acceptance are outside these automated results.
- Historical findings D1–D12 require individual current checks before any claim that all are resolved.

## QuantStudio melting comparison detail

The passing comparison log records 288 additional vendor peaks and 11,328 stored-versus-export derivative differences for one SYBR fixture. Passing means the test preserves and checks those declared representations; it does not mean every derivative value is identical. These differences need interpretation in their original test context, not suppression from a summary.

The passing comparison log records 288 additional vendor peaks and 11,328 stored-versus-export derivative differences for one SYBR fixture. Passing means the test preserves and checks those declared representations; it does not mean every derivative value is identical. These differences need interpretation in their original test context, not suppression from a summary.

## Attempt comparison

Initial and clean logs differ because the harness changed between attempts, not merely because instrumentation prints output. See HARNESS_ADJUSTMENTS.json and R2_SCOPE.md. PCRD keyboard passes cover password cancellation only.

The 3,688 entry observations are the preserved R1 instrumented snapshot. R2 runs are uninstrumented; ZIP contract evidence is linked separately and does not manufacture new hit counts.

pages.title: VoiceAndAudio
pages.text:
# Voice and audio

Say **Computer** or **Missy**, then finish the command. The workflow distinguishes a wake cue, completion of the command, acknowledgement/restatement and the data-backed answer. Navigation has its own confirmation cue. Repeated recognition events must not repeat an action.

Examples: “Computer, show chart two”; “Computer, next graph”; “Computer, status report”; “Computer, is there a problem?” Answers depend on loaded evidence. Unsupported causal claims and release approval must be refused.

The current index contains **122 command-registry entries**, **221 recorded English phrases** and **515 sound-catalogue entries**. These are different units: aliases, recorded speech and sound cues are not interchangeable counts. Some sound entries are deliberate silence/background paths.

The interface is bilingual, but the embedded recorded speech bank is English. Selecting Chinese does not translate these recordings. Dynamic speech also depends on locally installed voices. Microphone use and an offline language pack depend on browser capabilities. Typed commands provide an alternative in training.

Headless emulation checks routing and state transitions; it does not prove recognition accuracy with a real microphone or what an operator hears through speakers. Per-asset audio licensing must be reviewed separately from the source-code licence.

Download pseudonymisation does not govern speech. Spoken answers can contain identifiers regardless of the download setting and can be heard or recorded. Headphones do not make speech subject to that setting.

## Embedded asset accounting

The frozen HTML contains 221 audio/mpeg data URIs totalling 10,858,473 decoded bytes and 14,478,272 Base64 characters. See AUDIO_ASSET_REGISTER.json for every asset hash and location. Encoding metadata alone cannot establish which tool or source produced a recording. Exact hash matching links 194 clips to preserved creation records and a script selecting Microsoft Zira Desktop through Windows SAPI. The other clips are not thereby attributed. Applicable voice redistribution rights remain an open check; no clean-licensing claim is made. The sound catalogue is `window.MISSY_COMPUTER_SOUND.catalog` (515 entries); this differs from recorded phrase counts.
